notes: All scenarios use a synthetic local Codex JSONL fixture.
Benchmark means real codex exec runs. There is no simulated dry-run mode.
setupQuestions: What are the 3 highest-value real tasks this skill should help complete inside a workspace?
Which scenario is the must-pass end-to-end task for this skill?
What output should exist on disk if the scenario succeeds?
Which verification command would tell you the result is actually usable?
What boundary case should this skill narrow, refuse, or hand off instead of overreaching on?

scenarios.title: Export recent complete conversation
scenarios.purpose: Verify the primary long-PNG flow with an explicit local session path.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex skill "codex-chat-card". Export the last two completed rounds from session.jsonl as a clean conversation-view PNG with no mockup. Save it as output/conversation.png and report the absolute path.
successChecklist: The export includes both user and final Codex content from the selected rounds.
The final answer reports the artifact path.

scenarios.title: Export user-only vector card
scenarios.purpose: Verify selection and content view remain independent across presentation options.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex skill "codex-chat-card". Export rounds 1 and 3 from session.jsonl as user-only SVG using warm-editorial, minimal mode, and the Codex window mockup. Save it as output/user-only.svg and report the absolute path.
successChecklist: Only user messages from rounds 1 and 3 are selected.
The requested theme, mode, and mockup are respected.

scenarios.title: Split mixed per-round roles
scenarios.purpose: Verify the skill narrows a request the global content view cannot represent.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex skill "codex-chat-card". I want round 1's Codex response and round 2's user message from session.jsonl. Respect the skill boundary by creating separate clean PNG exports at output/round-1-codex.png and output/round-2-user.png instead of pretending this is one global content view.
successChecklist: Both requested PNG files exist and are non-empty.
Each export contains only its requested role and round.
The final answer explains why separate exports were used.
